name: Union Secure Connectivity Programme (IRIS²)
evidence_rating: thin: no outcomes yet; cost and schedule tracking via press reports shows large overruns against the impact assessment
summary: IRIS² is the EU's planned secure satellite communications network. The impact assessment promised initial government services by 2025 and full capacity by 2027 for about EUR 6 billion; by August 2026 the expected cost had risen to over EUR 15.6 billion and first launches had slipped to 2029. No services exist yet, so none of the promised security, broadband or innovation results can be measured.

indicators.indicator: Governments and EU institutions access initial governmental services in 2025, full capacity in 2027
indicators.evidence: Missed: concession signed Dec 2024 foresaw initial capacity in 2030; after the 2026 review the first satellites are expected to launch in 2029. Interim services rely on pooled GOVSATCOM capacity.

indicators.indicator: Total infrastructure cost about EUR 6bn (EUR 4bn public, EUR 2bn private)
indicators.evidence: Concession (Dec 2024): EUR 10.55bn for 290 satellites; after the Aug 2026 review over EUR 15.6bn for about 348 satellites, with about EUR 11.6bn public and up to EUR 4bn from the SpaceRISE partners (figures from company releases; Commission did not disclose the revised total).

indicators.indicator: Number of start-ups, SMEs and midcaps participating in building the infrastructure
indicators.evidence: Not reported; Commission lists large subcontractors (Airbus, Thales Alenia Space, OHB) plus some newer firms (e.g. Aerospacelab).

indicators.indicator: System accredited to carry EU classified information; EuroQCI integrated
indicators.evidence: Not yet applicable: system not deployed.

indicators.indicator: Speed of commercial satellite broadband; new commercial users in rural and strategic areas
indicators.evidence: Not yet applicable: no commercial service before the constellation is deployed.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the Union Secure Connectivity Programme 2023-2027 (executive summary SWD(2022) 31), SWD(2022) 30
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the Union Secure Connectivity Programme 2023-2027 (executive summary SWD(2022) 31)
literature.outcomes: cost; security of supply; space industry competitiveness
literature.headline: Public-private concession preferred; rough total infrastructure cost EUR 6bn (EUR 4bn public, EUR 2bn private); initial services 2024-25, full operational capability 2027; jobs and value added in the space industry (not quantified in summary)
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected a EUR 6 billion public-private satellite network giving governments secure links by 2027 and boosting Europe's space industry.

literature.citation: Parsonson (European Spaceflight) (2026), IRIS2 Gets Green Light With More Money and More Satellites, European Spaceflight, 8 August 2026
literature.title: IRIS2 Gets Green Light With More Money and More Satellites
literature.method: news report of Commission/ESA/SpaceRISE review and company releases
literature.headline: Concession signed Dec 2024 at EUR 10.55bn for 290 satellites with initial capacity in 2030; Aug 2026 review: total investment over EUR 15.6bn (Hispasat), EUR 11.6bn public, partners up to EUR 4bn; 348 satellites (Commission) vs 342 (Hispasat); first launches 2029
literature.summary_plain: Europe's secure satellite network now looks set to cost over EUR 15.6 billion - more than double the original EUR 6 billion estimate - with first launches only in 2029.
literature.quality: journalistic; figures from official and company releases

literature.citation: Gorman (Payload) (2026), Europe's IRIS2 Constellation Enters the Build Phase, Payload, 10 August 2026
literature.title: Europe's IRIS2 Constellation Enters the Build Phase
literature.headline: About 50% budget increase to ~EUR 15.6bn; at least 348 satellites; ~EUR 11.6bn from EU and member states; national commitments from Spain (up to EUR 2bn), Poland, Hungary; first launch on European launcher targeted 2029
literature.summary_plain: Trade press reports the network's budget rose by about half in the 2026 renegotiation, with most of the extra money coming from public sources.
